source_text: The persistence of Gishiri cutting among Hausa-Fulani communities in northern Nigeria stems from deeply held cultural beliefs that attribute obstructed labor, dyspareunia, and perceived vaginal narrowing—a condition termed "gishiri"—to supernatural or anatomical strictures requiring incision of the anterior vaginal wall for relief. [8]
